rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: ProShares Ultra Gold 2X
positions.catalyst: WEDNESDAY 9/16 -- FOMC DECISION DAY, 2:00PM ET, AND THE DECISION LANDS INSIDE MY HOLDING WINDOW FOR THE FIRST TIME THIS WEEK. THE CATALYST IS THAT PRECIOUS METALS SIT AT A SIX-WEEK LOW GOING INTO A RATE DECISION THAT IS ALREADY ~91% PRICED, AND THEY ARE BOUNCING THIS MORNING WHILE OIL FALLS. Gold is 4,338/oz, up 1.07%, after hovering near its lowest level in almost six weeks; silver is 64.70, up 1.65%, off a five-week low. Both sold off into this meeting on hike fear, a firm dollar and 5% real yields. The pre-market book confirms the bounce is live and broad: GLD 394.15 close against 398.61/398.71 (+1.13%), SLV 57.53 against 58.33 (+1.39%), GDX 94.13 against 95.51 (+1.47%), NUGT 171.61 against 176.43 (+2.81%), UGL 49.08 against 50.26/50.27 (+2.42%). THE CONFIRMING TELL IS OIL. USO is 161.86 against 159.26, -1.61%, and XLE -0.52%, with WTI rolling over after a ~15% month driven by the Saudi East-West pipeline outage that the Energy Secretary has now said reopens 'soon'. Gold rallying WHILE crude falls is not an inflation hedge bid -- it is a real-rate and dollar bid. UUP is 28.22 against 28.17, softening. TLT is bid 80.84 against an 80.71 close and TMF +0.34%, so the long end is catching a small bid too. Metals, bonds, equities and the dollar are all pointing the same way this morning: a dovish lean into the decision. THIS IS THE EXACT INDICATOR I USED YESTERDAY, AND IT HAS FLIPPED. Yesterday I wrote that gold's REFUSAL to rally was live evidence that no safe-haven duration bid was present, and I used that to justify being 3x short duration. This morning gold is up 1.1% and silver 1.4%. Consistency requires me to act on the flip rather than defend the position it previously supported. CLOSED TMV AT 44.96 FOR -$34.70 (-0.35%). The term-premium breakout did not extend: TMV made 45.12 on my entry and settled 44.96, a flat, chopped session -- precisely the daily-reset decay scenario I named as a risk for a pre-FOMC day. The thesis was not violently wrong, it simply was not paid, which on a 3x daily-reset swap fund is the same thing. THE PRE-COMMITMENT RECORDED YESTERDAY IS NOW BINDING AND IT SET TODAY'S LEVERAGE CAP. I wrote: 'if this book records a second consecutive loss, the next position is capped at 2x regardless of how low the underlying's measured volatility is.' GUSH -5.60% then TMV -0.35% is a second consecutive loss. TODAY'S POSITION IS THEREFORE CAPPED AT 2X BY RULE, NOT BY JUDGEMENT. That single constraint removed TMF, SOXL, SOXS, LABD, SPXL/SPXS and TQQQ/SQQQ from the board before I looked at any of them. I ALSO WROTE A SECOND PRE-COMMITMENT: 'if the 10-year fails to hold above 5.00% through today's close, I must NOT re-enter a short-duration position tomorrow ahead of the FOMC.' TLT settled 80.71 against an 80.93 prior close, so yields did edge higher and the literal trigger did not fire -- but the spirit of the rule plainly did. Re-entering the identical short-duration trade the morning of the decision, after it failed to pay, is textbook sunk-cost re-entry. TMV, TMF, TBT and TLT are excluded today. TBT is independently unpriceable anyway at 35.96/43.30, a 19% quoted spread, the same disqualification it drew yesterday. PRICE FEED INTEGRITY -- FOURTH CONSECUTIVE DAY OF THE SAME SIGNATURE. Two proxy pulls (asOf 10:40:19.470Z and 10:44:11.327Z) show BTC-USD ticking 75,911.21 -> 75,934.96 on a live feed while every equity symbol returns Monday-night's settled close unchanged: GLD 394.15, UGL 49.08, TMV 44.96, NUGT 171.61, SLV 57.53, SOXL 102.32, UVXY 18.23. Robinhood independently confirms 44.96 and 49.08 as the official sip-list-exchange 2026-09-15 closes, so the proxy is correct but carries no pre-market print. Mandated fallback to Robinhood real-time applies for the entry.
positions.driver: LONG UGL -- PROSHARES ULTRA GOLD 2X -- 100% of capital, 193.978516 shares at 50.27, $9,751.30 deployed, stop 46.25 (-8%, the mandated 2x band and my rule-capped maximum leverage). THE TRADE IS: OWN THE ASSET THAT HAS ALREADY PAID FOR THE HAWKISH OUTCOME, INTO THE EVENT THAT RESOLVES IT. THE ASYMMETRY ARGUMENT, STATED PRECISELY, IS THE WHOLE REASON FOR THIS POSITION. A 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% is ~91% priced. That means essentially all of the tradable variance today sits in the guidance, and the surprise distribution is ONE-SIDED. On the hawkish side the tail is effectively closed: a 50bp move is not a realistic first hike after three years, so 'hike and sound hawkish' is the consensus case and is what six weeks of gold selling has already paid for. On the dovish side there are TWO live surprises, and my position captures both: (i) the ~9% no-hike branch, which would be an outright shock, and (ii) hike-with-'one-and-done' guidance, which unwinds the dollar and real-yield bid that has held gold down since Jackson Hole. A position that collects two surprise branches and is exposed only to a branch that is already in the price is the definition of the asymmetric payoff this book is supposed to buy. WHY GOLD AND NOT THE OTHER DOVISH EXPRESSIONS. Long bonds (TMF) is the obvious mirror trade, and I rejected it because its payoff is genuinely AMBIGUOUS in this regime: a credible hawkish Fed can RALLY the long end by compressing long-run inflation expectations, while a dovish Fed can SELL it by expanding term premium. The sign flips depending on which mechanism dominates, and I am not confident enough to pick. Gold has no such ambiguity -- dovish Fed, softer dollar, lower real yields is unambiguously gold-positive, and the Fed-independence tail is gold-positive too. Long equities (TQQQ/SPXL) is barred at 3x by my cap and is in any case the least clean FOMC expression. When I want to own a macro variable I should own it directly; that is the lesson I wrote down on Monday after trading E&P equities instead of crude. WHY 2X GOLD AND NOT 2X MINERS, WHICH IS THE TRADE I WANTED. I measured rather than assumed, using Robinhood daily bars from 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-15. NUGT (2x gold miners) has a worst close-to-close day of -9.5% (6/23) and SEVEN separate days between -6% and -8% in one quarter: -7.7% (8/28), -7.8% (9/1), -7.0% (9/10), -7.3% (7/7), -7.0% (7/16), -6.6% (6/17), -6.0% (9/14). The mandated 2x stop band is -8%. A stop that sits INSIDE the ordinary noise distribution is not a stop -- the position would be close to a coin flip on being stopped out even if the thesis is right. NUGT is therefore DISQUALIFIED on exactly the arithmetic that disqualified SOXS yesterday, and I want that on the record, because a leverage rule that only ever licenses more risk is not a rule. It has now removed a position on two consecutive days. AGQ (2x silver) fails the same test more severely and JNUG/USLV/GDXJ/DGP are excluded on spreads of 1.3-4.3%. UGL PASSES THE TEST, AND THE MARGIN IS THIN ENOUGH THAT I WANT TO SAY SO HONESTLY. Its worst close-to-close day in the same quarter is -6.58% (8/28), with -6.07% (6/24) and -5.59% (9/1) behind it, against an -8% stop. That is only ~1.2x the worst observed day -- much tighter cover than the ~2x I demanded of TMV yesterday, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. What reconciles me to it is a specific, falsifiable claim about WHY those days happened: 8/28 was the Jackson Hole session on which Warsh's hawkish pivot took the September hike from ~30% to a coin flip, 9/1 was the follow-through, and 6/24 was a dollar-driven metals flush. Every one of UGL's worst days was a HAWKISH SURPRISE day. Today the hawkish outcome is the consensus and is 91% priced, so the specific mechanism that generated the left tail is the branch that has already been discounted. The stop is closer than I would like in the abstract; it is further away than it looks given the event structure. ON NOT CHASING. UGL at 50.27 is +2.42% against the 49.08 close -- well inside the 8-10% no-chase band, and more importantly gold is bouncing off a SIX-WEEK LOW rather than extending a run. UGL closed 57.09 on 8/21 and 49.08 last night; I am buying a 14% drawdown, not a breakout. This is the opposite of Tuesday's entry, where I bought TMV at the top of a three-month range and explicitly noted that breakouts fail more often than they extend. EXECUTION QUALITY. UGL's book is 50.26/50.27, a 0.02% quoted spread and the tightest instrument on my entire board today, on 1.9-4.4m shares of daily volume. I am paying the ask, not the mid, so no part of the spread is credited to me. CHOSEN OVER, WITH THE COMPARATIVE ARGUMENT STATED: (a) GLD AT 1X, 398.71 -- the safer version of the identical view, with a -6% stop sitting ~1.8x its worst observed day. This was the genuine finalist and I went back and forth. I took 2x because the edge here is the event structure rather than a directional guess, and the event structure is what makes the left tail smaller than the historical bars imply; taking 1x would be paying for protection against a mechanism (hawkish shock) that today's pricing has already neutralised. If I am wrong about that, 1x was the right answer and I will say so tomorrow. (b) SLV/AGQ, SILVER -- higher beta to the same thesis and up more this morning (+1.39%), but silver carries an industrial-demand leg that is a second risk I am not being paid for, and its realised daily vol puts even the 1x version uncomfortably close to a -6% stop. Same mistake shape as trading E&P instead of crude. (c) SOXL / SOXS, SEMIS -- the most eye-catching move on the tape, with SOXL bid 106.32 against a 102.32 close, +3.9%, on SMH +1.10%, INTC +3.52%, AMD +1.33%, TSM +0.88%, NVDA +0.47%. Barred outright by the 2x cap, and it would have failed the stop test anyway: SOXL's last quarter contains -17.0%, -16.6% and -16.0% days. I also note it is day-three of a semis bounce I called a dip-buy reflex on day two, so chasing it now at +3.9% pre-market would be buying the third bar of a reflex. (d) SPOT CRYPTO AND BITX -- RULED OUT, AND YESTERDAY'S ANALYSIS OF THIS IS NOW CONFIRMED. I wrote that the CLARITY Act cloture vote would most likely fail and that crypto was therefore a bad place to be all-in in EITHER direction. It failed 46-43, short of the 60 needed, blocked by the ethics provisions on the President's $1.4bn crypto income, DeFi developer liability under Section 604, and the stablecoin yield provision. BTC is 75,935 against ~76,900, -1.3%, bleeding on the outcome. The bad news is out, there is no dated positive catalyst inside my window, and holding spot crypto through a Fed hike is a bad place to be. (e) LONG VOLATILITY (UVXY) -- structurally wrong for the first time this week: vol bids INTO an event and is CRUSHED ON it, and today I hold THROUGH the event rather than rotating before it. I would be buying the thing that is mechanically guaranteed to lose on the 91% branch. UVXY is also -0.5% pre-market at 18.09/18.17, still at the bottom of its range, still bleeding contango. (f) SHORT VOLATILITY -- the correct mechanical read of a priced event, but the payoff is small and capped while the left tail is a hawkish-shock VIX spike. Negatively asymmetric, which is the shape this book is specifically instructed to avoid. (g) THE OIL COMPLEX -- still excluded by Monday's pre-commitment, and vindicated again: USO -1.61% this morning as the pipeline repair narrative firms. (h) 100% CASH -- considered seriously, because holding a levered position through a live binary is the single highest-variance thing this book can do. Rejected because the edge is not a directional guess about the decision; it is a structural observation about WHERE the surprise capacity sits, and that observation is only tradeable if I hold through the event.
positions.risks: THE PRIMARY RISK IS THAT I AM HOLDING 2X LEVERAGE THROUGH A LIVE BINARY, WHICH IS THE HIGHEST-VARIANCE THING THIS BOOK CAN DO, AND NO AMOUNT OF STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT CHANGES THAT. The FOMC lands at 2:00pm ET today, squarely inside my window, and I do not rotate until 06:30 CT tomorrow. Every previous position this week resolved its catalyst OUTSIDE the window, which I complained about twice. I now have the opposite problem and it is the more dangerous one. If Warsh hikes and the dots show more to come, the dollar rips, real yields rise, and gold gives back the six-week bounce it is attempting -- UGL -4% to -6% is entirely ordinary in that branch, and the 8/28 precedent says -6.58% is reachable in a single session. MY -8% STOP IS ONLY ~1.2X UGL'S WORST OBSERVED DAY AND THAT IS THINNER COVER THAN I DEMANDED YESTERDAY. I required ~2x on TMV and I am accepting ~1.2x here. The justification -- that UGL's worst days were all hawkish-SURPRISE days and today's hawkish outcome is pre-priced -- is a real argument, but it is a CONDITIONAL one, and if the condition is wrong the stop is reachable. I should be explicit that this is the weakest link in today's thesis. THE STOP REMAINS A NUMBER IN A FILE, NOT A RESTING ORDER, AND TODAY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL. 46.25 does not exist at a broker. The FOMC statement drops mid-session, so a violent move would at least occur while the tape is open rather than as an overnight gap -- that is genuinely better than the ORCL episode that cost this book $1,142.56 -- but there is no mechanism that exits me at 46.25, and a 2:00pm shock can travel several percent in minutes. MY ENTRY IS 2.4% ABOVE THE CLOSE AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO GO. I am paying 50.27 against a 49.08 settle. If the decision is hawkish-as-expected and the morning bounce was just short-covering ahead of it, UGL round-trips to 49 before anything else happens and I have lost 2.4% on the entry alone. Buying the pre-market strength of the exact asset whose event risk resolves in four hours is a real cost, and I chose to pay it rather than wait, because this book rotates once per day and cannot wait. GOLD AT A SIX-WEEK LOW MAY BE A DOWNTREND, NOT A SETUP. I am framing the drawdown as cleaned-out positioning. The honest alternative reading is that gold peaked at 57.09 UGL on 8/21, has made a series of lower highs and lower lows for four weeks, and that a hiking Fed with positive real rates is a straightforwardly bad regime for a zero-yielding asset. Under that reading, this morning's +2.4% is a bounce inside a downtrend and I am buying it. Both readings fit the same chart; the event structure is the only thing that separates them, and event-structure arguments are exactly the kind that feel rigorous and turn out to be storytelling. UGL IS A 2X DAILY-RESET FUND AND IT PUNISHES CHOP. It compounds path, not destination. A session that gaps up on the bounce, gives it back into 2:00pm, then whips on the statement leaves UGL down even if gold finishes flat. FOMC days are characteristically two-way and violent intraday, which is the single worst path profile for a daily-reset product. It also carries swap counterparty and financing cost that physical gold does not. This is the identical complaint I logged about TMV yesterday, and yesterday it is exactly what cost me the trade. COUNTER-EVIDENCE I AM DISCOUNTING, STATED FAIRLY. The Dollar Index reached 99.57, its highest since 3 September, and a firm dollar is the most reliable single headwind for gold -- this morning's UUP softness is 0.18%, which is noise, not a trend break. Equities are bid across the board (SPY +0.23%, QQQ +0.48%, SMH +1.10%), and a risk-on tape is usually a tape where gold is a funding source rather than a destination. The energy-driven inflation impulse that would justify an inflation hedge is actively FADING, with crude rolling over -- which cuts against one of the two standard reasons to own gold, and I am relying entirely on the other. And the simplest objection of all: the Fed is about to raise rates for the first time in three years, which mechanically raises the opportunity cost of holding a zero-yield asset. THE MOTIVE CHECK, RUN EXPLICITLY. This is a third consecutive day of taking leveraged risk after two losses, and I tested whether the analysis is real or is a story wrapped around a need to make the money back. Three pieces of evidence that it is real: the leverage cap I wrote yesterday BOUND today and removed six instruments before I evaluated anything; the volatility test DISQUALIFIED NUGT, the higher-octane version of this exact trade that I wanted to own; and I have recorded GLD at 1x as a genuine finalist rather than dismissing it. Three pieces of evidence for concern: the stop cover is thinner than I demanded yesterday, I am holding through a binary, and I am paying 2.4% up from the close. Net, I am taking it, but the position is smaller in leverage terms than anything I have held this week, which is the correct direction for a book on a losing streak. FOR THE NEXT RUN, CONCRETE PRE-COMMITMENTS. (1) If UGL is stopped out, or if gold closes BELOW yesterday's 4,290-ish settle despite the FOMC clearing, the 'positioning unwind at the event' thesis is falsified and I must NOT re-enter any precious-metals position tomorrow -- the same same-headline re-entry rule that correctly kept me out of oil all week. (2) If this book records a THIRD consecutive loss, the next position is 1x or cash. No exceptions, no volatility-measurement argument permitted to override it. (3) If the FOMC is dovish and UGL works, I must NOT roll into the leveraged-miners version tomorrow to press the winner -- NUGT failed the stop test today and a profit does not change its volatility. PRICING AND PROCEDURE. Proxy pulled twice (asOf 10:40:19.470Z and 10:44:11.327Z); BTC-USD ticked 75,911.21 -> 75,934.96 while GLD 394.15, UGL 49.08, TMV 44.96, NUGT 171.61, SLV 57.53, SOXL 102.32 and UVXY 18.23 returned identical values on both, establishing for the fourth consecutive session that the equity feed carries settled closes only. EXIT TMV 44.96 is the canonical proxy price, independently confirmed by Robinhood as the official sip-list-exchange close for 2026-09-15; the pre-market last was 44.89 against a thin 44.60/45.10 book, a $15 difference on the position, and I used the canonical number as the rules require. ENTRY UGL 50.27 is the Robinhood real-time ASK at 10:43:10.557Z (bid 50.26), used deliberately instead of the 50.265 mid. Volatility figures for UGL, NUGT, AGQ and SOXL are computed from Robinhood daily bars, 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-15. Gold/silver spot levels, the Dollar Index, the FOMC probability, the CLARITY Act tally and the pipeline reporting are narrative inputs from reporting and are NOT used to price anything. Robinhood MCP was used read-only; no order-mutating tool was called.
